title: Express on Node.js
description: For an HTTP service built with Express: supported versions, error handling, response headers, session cookies and login throttling.

rules.instruction: Run the service on an Active or Maintenance LTS release of Node.js and a maintained Express major version. Declare the Node.js range in `engines`.
rules.verification: Compare `engines.node`, the CI image and the Express version in the lockfile with the Node.js release table and the Express support notes.

rules.instruction: Let async handlers reject into a final four-argument error middleware that logs the error and returns a generic body. Run production with `NODE_ENV=production`.
rules.verification: Test a route that throws and assert a 500 response without a stack trace or internal message in the body.

rules.instruction: Set security response headers with Helmet or equivalent middleware, and disable the `X-Powered-By` header.
rules.verification: Assert the headers of a representative response in an HTTP test, including the absence of `X-Powered-By`.

rules.instruction: Give the session cookie a non-default name and set its `secure` and `httpOnly` options.
rules.verification: Inspect the `Set-Cookie` header returned by the login route in a test and check each attribute.

rules.instruction: Limit consecutive failed logins per user name and IP address, and failed attempts per IP address over a longer period.
rules.verification: Run a test that exceeds the limit and assert the blocked response, then check that a successful login is still possible after the window.

rules.instruction: Redirect only to paths or hosts on an allowlist when the target comes from the request.
rules.verification: Test the changed redirect with an external URL and assert that the response does not send the user there.
